 Storms could bring big hail and flash floods to New Mexico overnight into Saturday
 A severe thunderstorm watch covers most of New Mexico through 9 p.m. with wind gusts up to 70 mph, hail up to 3 inches and a flash flooding threat. ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. – A severe thunderstorm watch covers most of New Mexico through 9 p.m. with wind gusts up to 70 mph, hail up to 3 inches and a flash flooding threat.
 Some storms around the state could bring heavy rain and flash flooding Friday evening and overnight. Showers and storms could reach the Albuquerque area at times Friday evening and Friday night.
 Some of the heaviest rainfall may develop with storms later Friday night and Saturday in central and eastern New Mexico. They also warned rivers in the Four Corners area could crest at record high levels through Friday night.
 On Saturday, showers and storms could move through the Albuquerque metro area. More widespread showers and storms are expected in eastern New Mexico, where heavy rain could cause flash flooding along with hail and strong winds.
 By Sunday, most of the rain is expected to move out of western New Mexico, though some showers and storms may continue in eastern New Mexico. Mainly dry weather is expected across most of the state Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday.
 Rain chances may increase again toward next weekend.
